mutants.description: Copy-paste slip in the delay-flop block: hiccup_active_d is loaded from pwm_sync instead of hiccup_active, so hiccup_entry is no longer a single pulse on entry into S_HICCUP
mutants.reason: In S_HICCUP the PWM is stopped, so pwm_sync stays low and hiccup_entry = hiccup_active & ~pwm_sync_prev is true on every clock of the cool-down. strike_level then goes up every clock instead of once per hiccup, and latch_assert trips during the first hiccup instead of the MAX_STRIKES-th.

mutants.description: The strike clear tries to anticipate the clean-run counter reaching its target on the switching-cycle boundary, instead of waiting for the counter to actually hold clean_run_target
mutants.reason: strike_level drops to zero one clock earlier than it should. It is also cleared when the final PWM fall of the run comes on the same clock as a window_trip or the exit from S_RUN: the counter is then cleared rather than completed, so the run never earned the forgiveness.

mutants.description: A completed clean run clears latch_assert along with the strike count, as though forgiveness reset the whole protection state, although latch_assert is meant to be set-only and cleared by rst_n alone
mutants.reason: After latch_assert has tripped, a later stretch of clean_run_target fault-free switching cycles with run_active high deasserts latch_assert at the port. This input sequence is allowed by the module's own interface, though at top level the supervisor's S_OFF lock-out keeps run_active low after a latch.
